dedupe_keys.name: plateau traffic simulator for the traffic impact of commercial developments odaiba and aomi tokyo 2024

description: This Project PLATEAU use case of Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism developed tools that generate the input data for microscopic traffic simulation from open 3D city models, to lower the cost of assessing traffic impacts of large commercial and real estate developments. The Institute of Behavioral Sciences, i-Transport Lab and Synesthesias built a data generation tool that derives a road network (nodes, links, lengths, lanes and lane shapes near junctions) from PLATEAU road models, creates zones from building and terrain models, estimates existing and new origin-destination flows from cross-section and junction counts and floor areas, and reads signal timing open data from JARTIC; outputs are GeoJSON and CSV for the AVENUE simulator, and a 3D tool visualises vehicles and congestion. It was tested in December 2024 in Daiba (Minato) and Aomi (Koto), Tokyo. Developers reported a large workload reduction, and 14 municipal planners said the 3D view made congestion easier to understand, while asking for lane-level congestion and links to pedestrian flows. The report page is free to read; AVENUE is commercial software. It supports capacity planning and traffic impact assessment and is related to the JARTIC traffic volume data and PTV Vissim catalogued here.
